In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and function of WTA and LTA in B. subtilisis.
the synthesis of cell surface polymers in B. subtilisis and with the effect of tunicamicin on this process.
the role of WTA in cell wall assembly and cell growth, and the effect of tunicamicin in the cell wall of B. subutilis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tunicamycin inhibits WTA synthesis in B. subtils by interfering with the synthesis of poly(glucose 1-phosphate) and of poly(gro 1-phosphate).

tunicamycin is a specific inhibitor of poly(gro)P and poly(3-O-glucose)P synthesis in B. subtilisis, and that this inhibition is not accompanied by any detectable alteration in the synthesis of the major PG, LTA or P lipid components of the bacterial cell surface.
tunicamycin, at a concentration of 0.5-0.7 microg ml(-I) (MIC), inhibits poly(groP), poly(gal-galNAcP), and, to a lesser extent, poly(galP), but has no detectable effect on PG, LTA or P- lipids.

the fractionation procedure is specific, sensitive and reproducible.

the incorporation of [2- 3H]gro into poly(groP), LTA and P- lipid can be followed in B. subtili s, and that tunicamycin specifically and reversibly inhibits the synthesis of poly(3-0-beta-D-glucosyl-N-acetyl- galactosamine 2-phosphate), the major WTA of B. sub tilis.
